title: harness add must wire the ledger to git — bd init wires neither transport
description:
commands/add.sh runs 'bd init --prefix $prefix' and stops. bd's default .beads/config.yaml ships the export block commented out ('Optional JSONL auto-export ... Disabled by default'), so no .beads/issues.jsonl is ever written. Since .beads/embeddeddolt/ is gitignored, that means every bead a project files lives only in the local Dolt DB and NOTHING about the ledger reaches git. A fresh clone, a second machine, or a teammate gets an empty ledger.

psymail-mini works because its config.yaml was hand-edited three minutes after bd init (metadata.json Aug 10 19:10:42, config.yaml Aug 10 19:13:53) to add:

    sync.remote: "git+https://github.com/bubblesunyum/psymail-mini.git"
    export:
        auto: true

That hand edit is the step the harness extraction never captured. Proof it is the real transport: psymail-mini tracks .beads/issues.jsonl in git (119KB, committed alongside code in 99864ca, 1b57d85, 1f1cdf8...) and 'git ls-remote origin' on psymail-mini shows ONLY HEAD and refs/heads/master — there is no refs/dolt/data. Git is the transport; issues.jsonl is the payload.

Confirmed identical bug in control-center-pro, installed from this starter: diff of the two config.yaml files is exactly those four lines, and CCP had no issues.jsonl at all.
design: Append the block in add.sh right after the successful 'bd init'. sync.remote must be derived from the target's own 'git -C $target remote get-url origin', never hardcoded — psymail-mini's URL is in its config and must not propagate. Handle a repo with no origin yet: write the export block regardless (that is the part that matters for git transport) and skip sync.remote, or leave a clearly marked placeholder. Must stay idempotent — add.sh's contract is that re-running it is safe, so check for an existing 'export:' key before appending.
acceptance_criteria: After 'harness add' on a fresh repo, .beads/config.yaml contains an 'export: auto: true' block and a sync.remote pointing at that project's own git remote; .beads/issues.jsonl is generated and tracked by git. Verified by installing into a scratch repo, filing a bead, and confirming it appears in a committed issues.jsonl.
notes:
TESTED 2026-08-29 in control-center-pro: the Dolt transport works end to end, and it is the better one. Full sequence that was verified:

  bd dolt remote add origin "git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git"
  bd dolt commit -m "..."   # 'Nothing to commit' is fine, auto-commit is on
  bd dolt push               # -> creates refs/dolt/data on the GitHub remote

Verified by cloning the repo fresh, running 'bd init --prefix ccp', 'bd dolt remote add origin <url>', 'bd dolt pull'. The clone came back with all 37 issues, both bd remember memories, and full close reasons — WITHOUT the branch commits being pushed at all (origin/main was 4 commits behind). The Dolt ref carries the ledger independently of the branch.

Consequences for add.sh:
1. Writing sync.remote into config.yaml is NOT enough — 'bd dolt remote add' is a separate call and is what actually registers it.
2. A fresh clone does not get the ledger automatically. Onboarding is three commands (bd init / bd dolt remote add / bd dolt pull) and belongs in the starter's docs — see har-sul.
3. bd dolt push creates a visible 'refs/heads/__dolt_remote_info__' branch on the GitHub remote alongside refs/dolt/data. Cosmetic, but surprising in the GitHub branch dropdown; mention it so nobody deletes it.
4. Nothing runs 'bd dolt push' automatically — no beads git hooks are installed by this harness. It has to be in the session-close protocol or a hook, or the ledger silently stops syncing again.

Recommendation: wire BOTH. The jsonl export gives human-readable diffs in git and needs no setup on a clone; the Dolt remote carries memories, history and real merges. They are not exclusive.

title: session close must push the ledger — nothing runs bd dolt push automatically
description:
The Dolt transport works (see har-nqi, tested), but it is entirely manual. This harness installs no beads git hooks — .git/hooks/ in both psymail-mini and control-center-pro contains at most the harness's own commit-msg shim, and beads' pre-push hook (which would sync on git push) is never installed. add.sh:154 deliberately avoids .git/hooks because beads rewrites that directory on upgrade.

So a session can file beads, close beads, commit, git push, and leave the Dolt ledger a full session behind, with no signal that it happened. That is the same class of silent drift as har-nqi, just one layer up.

psymail-mini is the live proof: sync.remote has been configured there since Aug 10 with a registered Dolt remote, and 'git ls-remote origin' still shows no refs/dolt/data. Correctly configured, never pushed, for three weeks.
design: Cheapest honest option is a check rather than an action: have the brief or verify.sh compare the local Dolt commit against the remote ref and print one line when they differ. Pushing on the user's behalf at session close is a bigger call and should stay opt-in — the repo profile is conservative about outward-facing actions by default.
acceptance_criteria: A session cannot end with an unpushed ledger without being told. Either the session-close protocol in CLAUDE.snippet names 'bd dolt push' explicitly, or the harness runs it, or verify.sh reports the ledger as ahead of its remote.
notes: Depends on har-nqi landing the remote registration first.

title: bd remember memories never reach git — the export omits them by design
description:
The JSONL export that carries the ledger to git contains only issues. Memories written with 'bd remember' — the ones the session brief surfaces every session as 'known traps' — stay in the local Dolt DB and reach no clone.

Measured in control-center-pro:
  grep _type .beads/issues.jsonl  ->  37 "_type":"issue", 0 memory records
  bd export --all -o /tmp/all.jsonl  ->  37 issue + 2 memory records
  .beads/export-state.json literally reads {"issues":37,"memories":0}

Both of CCP's memories are real load-bearing knowledge (the Permissions.swift 1336-error trap, the SwiftUI-import undercount) and neither is in git.

The export config block bd init ships exposes auto/path/interval/git-add — no option to include memories. So this is not a setting that was missed; the auto-export path cannot carry them.

This matters more for the harness than for beads generally: CLAUDE.snippet tells every project 'Use bd remember for persistent knowledge — do NOT use MEMORY.md files'. The harness actively directs knowledge into the one store that does not survive a clone.
design: 'bd export --all -o .beads/issues.jsonl' would carry both, but check whether bd import round-trips memory records before adopting it — a file the auto-export then overwrites with an issues-only version would silently drop them again. A separate tracked .beads/memories.jsonl may be safer since auto-export owns issues.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: Either memories ride to git (an explicit 'bd export --all' step writing a tracked file), or the harness stops telling projects that bd remember is durable and says plainly that memories are machine-local.
notes: Resolved differently than this bead assumed: memories DO survive if the Dolt transport is used. Verified by clone in har-nqi — 'bd dolt pull' into a fresh clone returned both of control-center-pro's memories. The JSONL export still omits them, so this bead now reads: if a project relies on the jsonl export alone, bd remember is machine-local and CLAUDE.snippet's 'use bd remember for persistent knowledge' is false for it. Wiring the Dolt remote (har-nqi) is the fix; this bead is the docs/telling-the-truth half.

title: bd export is incremental — a stale issues.jsonl can be committed without anyone noticing
description:
With 'export: auto: true' set, .beads/issues.jsonl is not written synchronously on every bd mutation. Measured in control-center-pro: filing a bead left issues.jsonl byte-identical; a following 'bd export' still did not contain it (export-state.json carries a last_dolt_commit high-water mark and only emits what has advanced past it); a second 'bd export' picked it up. Deleting a bead is worse — the deleted issue stayed in issues.jsonl through repeated 'bd export' runs, and only a full regeneration (rm .beads/issues.jsonl .beads/export-state.json && bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl) produced a correct file.

Consequence: a session can close beads, commit, and push a issues.jsonl that is missing the closes or still lists deleted work. The ledger silently disagrees with itself across machines, which is the exact failure the ledger exists to prevent.
design: Cheapest correct option is a full regeneration rather than an incremental export, since the file is small (43KB / 37 issues in CCP, 120KB in psymail-mini) and incremental export demonstrably does not handle deletes. A pre-commit hook is the natural home, but note scripts/hooks/ is the harness's own directory — .beads/hooks/ is managed by beads and gets rewritten on upgrade, and add.sh already comments on that trap at line 154. Alternative: fold it into verify.sh so the gate fails on a stale export.
acceptance_criteria: The harness guarantees a fresh, correct issues.jsonl reaches every commit that touches the ledger — via a pre-commit step, a verify.sh check, or an explicit step in the session-close protocol. Verified by deleting a bead and confirming the committed issues.jsonl no longer contains it.
notes:
Refined after reading the config schema in .beads/config.yaml (the commented block bd init ships). The export block supports more than 'auto':

    export:
      auto: false
      path: issues.jsonl
      interval: 60s
      git-add: false

'interval: 60s' explains the lag measured in control-center-pro — auto-export is a timer, not a per-mutation write, so a bead filed and committed inside the same minute misses the export. The original framing (high-water mark alone) was incomplete: it is a 60s timer AND incremental semantics that does not drop deleted issues.

'git-add: true' is likely the cheapest half of the fix — it stages issues.jsonl automatically so a session cannot forget it. Neither psymail-mini nor CCP sets it. That still leaves deletes needing a full regen.

Separately: the export block exposes no option to include memories, and the default export omits them — see har-jx2.

Blocked by har-nqi.

title: dashboard: a dropped poll blanks the whole repaint
description: tick() in dashboard/index.html wraps the fetch AND all ten draw calls in one try. A single dropped fetch jumps to the catch, paints the pulse offline, and skips the entire repaint, so the board silently keeps whatever it last drew — which is what 'the dashboard stopped showing new beads and commits' looks like from outside. Split the fetch out of the draw try/catch: a transient fetch failure should touch the pulse indicator and nothing else. Keeping the last good payload and redrawing from it would be better still. Diagnosed in control-center-pro as ccp-not; the code is this starter's.
notes: Overlaps work in flight: har-whx.1 added 'runStates = d.runs || {}' as the first line inside tick()'s try, before drawRuns(). When the fetch is split out, that assignment belongs with the fetch's success path, not with the draws — every run button on the page is drawn from it.

title: dashboard falls behind its own polling
description: Diagnosed in control-center-pro (bead ccp-not), but the code is this starter's, so every install has it. state() takes 2.5-3.1s to build while CACHE_TTL is 4.0s and the page polls every 2500ms, so the cache expires between polls and the server regenerates on roughly every other request — a ~75% duty cycle of continuous bd and git shell-outs. Each miss holds _lock, so a poll landing inside a generation blocks up to 3s; on a 2.5s cadence responses back up until the browser drops the connection, leaving BrokenPipeError in the dash log. Agent bd commands in a terminal make it worse: the dashboard's own bd calls contend with them on the embedded Dolt lock, so generation slows exactly when the ledger is changing. Of the 2.5-3.1s, ledger_state is ~0.88s across three bd shell-outs (bd ready, bd list --all --limit 0, bd stale --days 14), each spinning up its own Dolt engine.
design: Regenerate on a background timer and serve the last snapshot immediately, so do_GET never blocks. That removes the collision rather than retuning it. If on-demand generation is kept instead, CACHE_TTL has to exceed the poll interval by more than one generation cost — better, derive it from how long the last generation actually took.
acceptance_criteria: Eight curls two seconds apart all return fast, with no alternating multi-second spikes. A burst of bd commands in a terminal leaves the pulse live and the board tracking. No BrokenPipeError in the dash log.

title: dashboard gate reads every passing step as failed
description: verify_state() in scripts/dashboard.py decides a step passed with: ok = bool(text.strip()) and not re.search(r'\\berror:', text). But step() in scripts/verify.sh writes the command's output to the log and a passing step produces an EMPTY log, so bool(text.strip()) is False and every green step is read as failed. Result: scripts/verify.sh prints 'verify: passed' and the dashboard header says 'failing' with all steps red, permanently. Confirmed 2026-08-29: run state 'ok' and gate status 'failed' in the same state.json. The empty-log guard exists to stop a step that never ran from reading green, so the fix is not to drop it — verify.sh knows each step's exit status and should record it (a per-step status file next to the log), with the text heuristic as the fallback for projects whose tools print a verdict.
acceptance_criteria: A passing scripts/verify.sh leaves the dashboard header reading 'verified'. A step that never ran still does not read as passed.

title: review packet can't see the dashboard page
description: SCOPE in scripts/review.sh:47 lists '*.py' '*.sh' '*.md' and some paths, but not '*.html'. dashboard/index.html is the largest file in the project and where most dashboard work lands, and no reviewer has ever seen a line of it. Same class as the bug the comment right above SCOPE describes for bin/ and commands/. dashboard/vendor/* is already excluded, so adding '*.html' picks up the page and nothing else.
close_reason: *.html added to SCOPE in both copies; HARNESS.md and the agentic-review skill updated to match. 6639e73

title: harness add ships untracked junk from template/
description: commands/add.sh:113 lists files with 'find $TEMPLATE -type f', which ignores .gitignore. A working starter checkout that has run the dashboard has template/scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc, so the installer tries to sed a binary file. Under LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 — which every Python parent sets, including the dashboard's own verify button — BSD sed fails with 'RE error: illegal byte sequence', and add.sh dies partway through the copy leaving a half-installed project. From a plain terminal (locale unset) sed is byte-wise and it passes, so the gate is green by hand and red from the dashboard. Fix: source the file list from git (tracked + untracked-not-ignored), so the product is what the repo says it is.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/verify.sh passes under LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8. A .pyc in template/scripts/__pycache__ is never installed.
close_reason: File list from git ls-files, plus an up-front check that every listed file is on disk. ce68237

title: harness update dashboard
description: A dashboard-scoped update, deliberately NOT a whole-harness update: overwriting other harness files in an existing project needs a guided process of its own. Re-copies dashboard/ and scripts/dashboard.py from the starter checkout, never touches dashboard.toml. harness add stays never-overwrite (commands/add.sh:98). Also fixes the self-hosting drift README calls out at README.md:105 for these files.

title: dashboard: run table to dashboard.toml, project/prefix at runtime
description: Move the run table out of dashboard.py into a dashboard.toml the update never touches (tomllib, stdlib). Move {{PROJECT}}/{{PREFIX}} install-time substitution to runtime lookup so shipped files are byte-identical everywhere.

title: dashboard: one run-button table, server-side
description: The run buttons are configured in four places that must agree: TASKS in scripts/dashboard.py (commands), const TASKS + RUN_LABEL in dashboard/index.html (header strip), a hardcoded push button in the staging lane, and a hardcoded verify button in the gate pane. Collapse to one server-side table carrying command, label, busy label and placement; the page renders slots from d.runs and names no task.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a run button means editing TASKS in dashboard.py only. No task key appears in index.html.
close_reason: One server-side TASKS table carries command, label, busy and placement; page renders slots via runButton/runSlot and names no task. c04e698

title: README and CLAUDE.snippet never tell a project how its ledger reaches git
description:
The starter README's 'What you get' table describes the ledger as 'beads in .beads/ — work and discoveries survive the session that found them'. Survival across sessions on one machine is true even when broken; survival across clones is the part that was silently absent, and nothing in the README, AGENTS.md, or the post-install instructions in add.sh says .beads/issues.jsonl is the transport or that it must be committed.

The post-install block in add.sh lists four things 'no script can infer' (seat.md, CLAUDE.snippet.md, verify.sh PROJECT STEPS, the reviewer agent files). Ledger transport was a fifth and it was not on the list, so it was never done.

Worse, the managed beads block that lands in CLAUDE.md states: 'issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses refs/dolt/data on your git remote; .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export.' In this harness that is backwards — neither psymail-mini nor control-center-pro has a refs/dolt/data ref on origin, and issues.jsonl is the only thing carrying the ledger. An agent reading that block reaches for 'bd dolt push', which is not how these projects sync.
acceptance_criteria: A reader of the starter can state, without reading beads' source, how their ledger gets from their machine to their remote. If the managed beads block's refs/dolt/data claim cannot be corrected in place (it is rewritten by beads on upgrade), the harness's own docs say plainly what actually happens and that the managed block is wrong on this point.
notes: Found while diagnosing har-nqi: the wrong mental model from that block cost a real session's worth of debugging in control-center-pro.

title: add.sh reports success it never verified — 'initialised the ledger' can be a lie
description:
commands/add.sh:188 treats a zero exit from 'bd init --prefix $prefix' as the ledger being ready and prints 'initialised the ledger ($prefix-)'. It never checks that the ledger is actually usable or that the pieces the harness depends on exist. That is how control-center-pro reached a state where every session printed a healthy-looking brief while the ledger had no git-visible representation whatsoever.

The script already shows this instinct elsewhere and it pays off — the comment at :183 explains that keying on '.beads existing' would report an uninitialised ledger as initialised, 'which is how you find out later, one failing bd at a time'. That reasoning stops one step short: it validates that a prefix came back, not that the ledger works.

Compounding it: 'bd doctor', which is the tool that would normally catch a misconfigured ledger, refuses to run in embedded mode — it prints 'not yet supported in embedded mode' and exits. Embedded is what bd init produces by default, so the starter's projects are exactly the ones doctor cannot help.
design: Keep it to a couple of cheap assertions so install stays fast: 'bd stats' or 'bd list' returning cleanly, plus a grep for the export block once har-nqi lands. Do not shell out to bd doctor — it is unavailable in embedded mode, which is the default this installer produces.
acceptance_criteria: add.sh verifies the ledger after init — at minimum that a bead can be filed and read back, and that the configuration the harness relies on is present — and reports the real state rather than the exit code. A failed verification prints what to run to fix it.

title: design review can't see any hover state
description: scripts/dashboard.py shot photographs the page as it loads, so every capture the design reviewer ever reads is the default view. The dashboard puts real content behind hover and focus — the gate popover (which now holds a run button), the pulse tip, the lane stage tips, the file menu, the commit composer. None of it has ever been reviewed, and reviewer-design correctly refused to sign off on the run-button rework for exactly this reason: the only placement it could see was the empty one. Verified by hand on 2026-08-29 instead, driving the page in the browser pane, because the harness could not produce the captures. Wants 'shot' to take a list of states to photograph — an element to focus or hover before each capture — writing one /tmp/har-*.png per state so the packet carries them all.

title: dashboard: ledger_state spins up three Dolt engines per build
description: ledger_state in scripts/dashboard.py makes three separate bd calls — bd ready, bd list --all --limit 0, bd stale --days 14 — each spinning up its own embedded Dolt engine, together ~0.88s of a 2.5-3.1s state build. bd list --all already carries labels, description, design and notes; check whether ready-ness and staleness can be derived from that one payload instead of two more engine spin-ups. Diagnosed in control-center-pro as ccp-not.

title: dashboard: package as its own unit with a README
dashboard: panels vanish cleanly when their source is missing
description: No bd on PATH means no ledger lanes; no .claude/ means no harness panel; no verify logs means no gate. Absence as a first-class state, not an empty or confused shape. Root via git rev-parse --show-toplevel with a cwd fallback instead of the script's own path.

title: extract the dashboard as a standalone, adaptable package
notes: Hard requirement: dashboard is developed here and must update in place across every project that installed it. That makes 'shipped files are byte-identical everywhere' the load-bearing constraint — all per-project variation must live in a config file + runtime detection, never in edits to dashboard.py/index.html and never in install-time {{PROJECT}}/{{PREFIX}} substitution (dashboard.py:93,319,1048,1060,1079; index.html:6,1529 — all derivable at runtime). Then update = delete + re-copy, no merge. Needs a 'harness update' command; 'harness add' deliberately never overwrites (commands/add.sh:98).

title: dashboard backgrounds by default; portside alias in the announce
close_reason: default backgrounds via serve child; portside alias printed when the map matches port+directory

title: dashboard always opens in claude code's browser
close_reason: dashboard.py publishes launch.json + prints the pane instruction; no system browser path left

title: dashboard: two racing `up` calls both print 'started on 7391'
close_reason: fixed with the psymail backport: up now passes --port to the child that binds, and the bare path treats a failed bind as 'someone got here first' instead of asking holder() and acting on a stale answer. Both copies in step

title: self-host: finish the harness-starter install (CLAUDE.md, verify gate, seat, reviewer traps)
close_reason: self-hosted the starter: bin/harness frees the harness/ name the template needs, self-install guard removed, and the root now carries a working install with CLAUDE.md, a real gate (parse + probe-install + CLI), the Tern seat, and reviewer traps from this session. Review found the placeholder check passing vacuously when its own setup failed, and the *.md scope widening applied to the root copy but not the template — both fixed
